costNote: Fuel burned and power bought to serve customers, $2,087M — the utility's direct cost. Demand from new data centers is pulling this (and revenue) up fast.

opex.note: A huge, fast-growing asset base: AEP just lifted its five-year capital plan to $100B.

opex.note: Keeping plants and lines in shape.

otherDetail.note: A regulated-utility credit: the deemed return on equity money tied up in construction projects.

otherDetail.note: $6M other income, $25M of non-service pension credits and $25M of equity earnings from unconsolidated subsidiaries (which AEP reports after tax).

footerNote: Utility layout: fuel and purchased electricity are the direct-cost block; figures are from AEP's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q. Net income is the consolidated $1,218M; $1,187M was attributable to AEP common shareholders after noncontrolling interests.

oneTimers.label: GAAP vs operating
oneTimers.text: The $29M gap between GAAP earnings ($1,187M) and operating earnings ($1,216M) is mainly mark-to-market on risk-management positions — AEP strips it from its headline measure.

segments.name: Vertically Integrated Utilities
segments.note: Generation + delivery in states like Ohio, West Virginia and Oklahoma — where the data-center load boom is landing. 15 GW of new load commitments signed in Q3 alone.

segments.name: Transmission & Distribution Utilities
segments.note: Wires-only utilities (incl. Texas) that buy power and deliver it. AEP is the largest US transmission owner; transmission rate base is set to nearly double by 2031.

segments.name: Generation & Marketing
segments.note: Competitive generation and wholesale marketing — up 33% on power-market demand.

takeaways.text: AEP's contracted incremental load is expected to reach 84 GW by 2031 under signed agreements — an enormous data-center and industrial pipeline for an 11-state utility.
takeaways.title: The load queue is the story

takeaways.text: The five-year capital plan jumped to $100B (rate base CAGR 13%+, to $162B by 2031), underpinning guided operating EPS growth of 9–11% a year for 2027–2031.
takeaways.title: Capex super-cycle

takeaways.text: Take-or-pay contracts with large new customers are expected to offset up to $21B of fixed costs for existing residential customers — AEP's answer to the 'data centers raise my bill' argument.
takeaways.title: Affordability pitch

verdict: AEP is the data-center power play among utilities: revenue up 14%, a $100B build plan, and 9–11% guided EPS growth.
